task_3_first_buyer.ready_to_post:
Worth adding for anyone who ends up here the same way I did - the part that actually unlocked it for me was deciding what to write down FIRST, before contacting the insurer.

Three numbers, not one: the 17c figure, the median gap from 5-8 same-year/trim/mileage comps (half clean-history, half accident-flagged), and a dealer trade-in letter. The carrier will only engage with the comps and the letter; 17c alone reads as a formula argument and gets declined.

Mileage adjustment band people mention is roughly $0.15-0.25/mile - state yours explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

Before signing anything from the insurer: check whether the release says 'all claims' or specifically property-damage repair costs, whether diminished value is reserved anywhere, and whether the check has a deadline that implies acceptance. Signing 'all claims' quietly ends the conversation.

One flag - before/after values have to be established BEFORE you accept any settlement, and several states have short property-damage deadlines. That part is genuinely time-sensitive and worth checking against your own state rules early.
